title: Appendix D — Four Master Tropes

outline.thesis: The four tropes — metaphor, metonymy, synecdoche, irony — are not figures of speech but instruments for the discovery and description of 'the truth'. Their literal-realistic substitutions are perspective, reduction, representation, dialectic. The four shade into one another: any one trope, fully developed, generates the other three.
key_moves: Announces the four substitutions in a table (metaphor=perspective; metonymy=reduction; synecdoche=representation; irony=dialectic)

Establishes the inter-transformability principle: a dialectic gives representation by interacting perspectives, and the resulting perspective-of-perspectives is itself a reduction (scale-chart analogy)
Footnote: 'dialectic' is used in the restricted sense; in the broader sense all the transformations in the essay are dialectical

outline.thesis: Metaphor is the device for seeing something in terms of something else — bringing out the thisness of a that, or the thatness of a this. To consider A from the point of view of B is to use B as a perspective on A.
key_moves: Introduces 'character' as Burke's general placeholder for whatever can be thought of as distinct (thing, pattern, situation, structure, nature, person, object, act, role, process, event)

Argues that objective reality is not dissolved by relativity-of-terms; rather, a character's reality is established by approaching it through a variety of perspectives (lifting, smelling, tasting, tapping, holding in different lights)

Poetic-realist axiom: characters possess degrees of being in proportion to the variety of perspectives from which they can with justice be perceived (plants > minerals; animals > plants; men > animals)
Open list of motive-perspectives offered as random examples: conditioned reflexes, chemicals, class struggles, love of God, neurosis, pilgrimage, power, planetary motion, geography, sun spots
Cross-reference to Permanence and Change: metaphor as 'incongruity' and the 'carrying-over' of a term across realms

outline.thesis: The basic strategy of metonymy is to convey some incorporeal or intangible state in terms of the corporeal or tangible (e.g., 'heart' for 'emotions'). Trail any 'spiritual' term back far enough and you find a metonymic origin. Reduction is the metonymic move proper to scientific realism; metonymy proper is the device of poetic realism.
key_moves: Diagnoses science qua science as concerned with correlation, not substance — and therefore unfit for motivation, which is a substantial question
Argues that any attempt to handle human relations after the analogy of naturalistic correlations becomes a reduction of a higher realm of being to the terms of a lower one

Two-direction history of language: corporeal terms metaphorically extend into the incorporeal; the corporeal origin is forgotten; the poet 'archaicizes' by extending the incorporeal back into a tangible equivalent — this archaicizing move is metonymy

Distinguishes poetic from scientific behaviorism: both translate the spiritual into bodily equivalents, but the poet treats the bodily as 'figures' / 'symbolizations' (not substantial reductions), whereas the scientific behaviorist offers his reduction as a 'real' reduction (qua materialist metaphysics, not qua scientist)
Pivot to synecdoche: a reduction is a representation (relief-map example), so metonymy overlaps synecdoche

outline.thesis: Synecdoche covers the full dictionary range (part-for-whole, whole-for-part, container-for-contained, sign-for-thing-signified, material-for-thing-made, cause-for-effect, effect-for-cause, genus-for-species, species-for-genus). All such conversions imply an integral relationship of convertibility. The 'noblest synecdoche' is the microcosm-macrocosm identity of metaphysical doctrine. Metonymy is a special, one-direction case of synecdoche.
key_moves: Leibniz's monadology cited as the grand-scale paradigm of synecdochic identity (and 'representation' is Leibniz's own word for it)
Political representation: any act of representation in a complex civilization automatically implies a synecdochic relationship — Rousseau's volonté générale named as paradigm
Sensory representation is synecdochic: the senses abstract qualities (size, shape, color, texture, weight) from the electro-chemical bundle we call a tree; these qualities 'truly represent' the tree

Artistic representation is synecdochic: relations within the medium 'stand for' relations outside it; the well-formed work of art is internally synecdochic (beginning contains close; close sums beginning)
Deliberate 'coaching' of the synecdochic concept to cover reversible pairs: before/after, implicit/explicit, temporal/logical sequence, name/narrative, disease/cure, hero/villain, active/passive

Worked examples: Coleridge's Ancient Mariner — 'the Albatross is a gerundive' (its nature when introduced is that-which-is-to-be-murdered; implicit contains explicit future). Moby-Dick: Ahab as pursuer is pursued; his action is a passion
Direction asymmetry: synecdoche/representation is two-way; metonymy/reduction is one-way (quality-to-quantity only, in the restricted sense)
Footnote-based amendment: in the broader sense, every consideration of A in terms of B is a 'referring-back' and so a 'reduction-as-perspective'
Otto Neurath's isotypes cited as reductive (quantitative) representations contrasted with realistic portrait-painting (qualitative representation)

Tactical-error diagnosis: the mathematico-quantitative ideal of the physical sciences misapplied to social sciences produces 'fabulous amassing of statistical surveys' that mistakes a reductive anecdote for a representative anecdote
Korzybski's 'Structural Differential' (contraption of string, plugs, tin) and Thurman Arnold's psychiatric metaphor of social relations are named as reductive misrepresentations

outline.thesis: Irony is the trope of dialectic: it arises when one tries, by the interaction of terms upon one another, to produce a development that uses all the terms. From the standpoint of this total form (the 'perspective of perspectives'), none of the participating sub-perspectives can be treated as either precisely right or precisely wrong; they are all voices, integrally affecting one another.
key_moves: Equates dialectic with 'dramatic': where ideas are in action, drama; where agents are in ideation, dialectic — 'Socratic irony' is dramatic; 'dramatic irony' is Socratic

Distinguishes irony from relativism: relativism is got by the fragmentation of either drama or dialectic — taking any one agent's position as the whole. In relativism there is no irony (and Cleanth Brooks's observation: relativism's monologic absolutism is itself maximally susceptible to irony)

Names three temptations of irony: (a) collapse into relativism; (b) Pharisaic 'superiority' (romantic irony as opposed to true / classic / humble irony); (c) simplification of literalness (the primus-inter-pares character forgotten as both adjectival qualifier and substantial representative)

Critique of Allen Tate on Eliot's Waste Land seduction scene: Tate calls the poet's attitude 'humility' but Burke argues Eliot is congratulating himself for not being like the petty clerk — this is Pharisaic, not humble, irony
Newton vs. the criminal: 'that man is going to prison for me' — true irony-and-humility because Newton is simultaneously outside the criminal and within him
True irony as consubstantiality: based on a sense of fundamental kinship with the enemy — Flaubert's 'Madame Bovary, c'est moi'; Thomas Mann's 'Judas psychology'; Anatole France
Romantic irony vs. classic irony: Eliot's religious problem framed as the conversion of romantic to classic irony (Murder in the Cathedral as ritual of motive-purification)
Dialectic irony as 'technical equivalent for the doctrine of original sin': folly and villainy are integral motives, necessary to wisdom or virtue

Long footnote on Falstaff (gloriously ironic) vs. Tartuffe (not ironic, pure hypocrite) — Falstaff identifies with the victim, sympathetic-distortion of religious values; Tartuffe merely simulates cooperation

Marxism example: 'slavery is bad' in literal libertarian rhetoric, but from the standpoint of the development as a whole, slavery must be treated ironically (Engels: 'Without the slavery of antiquity, no modern socialism')
Proletariat as 'the Socrates of the Marxist Symposium of History' — both an adjectival qualifier and substantial representative of the development as a whole

outline.thesis: Irony moves us into the area of 'law' and 'justice' (the necessity / inevitability of the lex talionis). The over-all ironic formula: 'what goes forth as A returns as non-A' — the basic pattern that places the essence of drama and dialectic in the irony of the peripety, the strategic moment of reversal.
key_moves: Predictive richness of ironic generalization in history: that what arises in time must in time perish; that the developments leading to the rise will lead to the fall (true irony as 'internal fatality')

Casuistries appear at the level of fitting general inevitability-laws to unique historical cases — exactly which new characters, born of a given prior character, become the 'inevitable vessels' of its deposition
Master ironic formula: A → non-A (the peripety)

concepts.label: Trope (master)
concepts.gloss: Operation for the discovery and description of the truth, not merely a figure of speech.

concepts.label: Metaphor
concepts.gloss: Device for seeing something in terms of something else; brings out the thisness of a that.

concepts.label: Perspective
concepts.gloss: Literal-realistic substitution for metaphor: to consider A from the point of view of B.

concepts.label: Metonymy
concepts.gloss: Conveys an incorporeal or intangible state in terms of the corporeal or tangible; the 'archaicizing' device.

concepts.label: Reduction
concepts.gloss: Metonymic move proper to scientific realism: explains higher orders by reduction to lower orders; one-direction (quality-to-quantity).

concepts.label: Synecdoche
concepts.gloss: Convertibility relation between part and whole, container and contained, sign and signified, etc.

concepts.label: Representation
concepts.gloss: Two-way convertibility between parts and wholes; 'noblest synecdoche' is microcosm-macrocosm identity.

concepts.label: Irony
concepts.gloss: Arises from the interaction of all the terms; perspective of perspectives in which sub-perspectives are voices, neither right nor wrong.

concepts.label: Dialectic
concepts.gloss: Where agents are in ideation; equatable with the dramatic. Restricted sense (this essay) vs broader sense (all four transformations are dialectical).

concepts.label: Perspective of perspectives
concepts.gloss: The resultant total form when terms interact; necessarily a reduction (scale-chart) and the home of irony.

concepts.label: Character (Burkean)
concepts.gloss: General placeholder for anything thinkable as distinct: thing, pattern, situation, structure, nature, person, object, act, role, process, event.

concepts.label: Degrees of being
concepts.gloss: Poetic-realist axiom: characters possess being in proportion to the variety of perspectives from which they can be justly perceived.

concepts.label: Poetic realism
concepts.gloss: Burke's term for substance-centered, motivation-oriented realism, contrasted with scientific (correlation-only) realism.

concepts.label: Scientific realism
concepts.gloss: Correlation-oriented, substance-evasive, reduces higher orders to lower; its trope is reduction proper.

concepts.label: Microcosm–macrocosm identity
concepts.gloss: Noblest synecdoche: individual as replica of universe and vice versa; Leibniz's monadology as paradigm.

concepts.label: Carrying-over (metaphor-as-incongruity)
concepts.gloss: Transfer of a term across realms; the two realms are never identical, hence varying degrees of incongruity.

concepts.label: Corporeal–incorporeal axis
concepts.gloss: Two-direction metonymic history: language builds incorporeal vocabulary from corporeal terms; poet reverses the carry-over.

concepts.label: Representative anecdote
concepts.gloss: A terminology of conceptual analysis must be constructed in conformity with a representative anecdote; reductive anecdotes are not representative.

concepts.label: Relativism (vs. irony)
concepts.gloss: Fragmentation of drama or dialectic; isolates one agent's position; absence of irony makes it maximally susceptible to it.

concepts.label: Romantic irony
concepts.gloss: Pharisaic / superior stance; artist outside and above the rejected role; opposed to philistinism.

concepts.label: Classic / true / humble irony
concepts.gloss: Based on consubstantiality with the enemy; one is indebted to, needs, contains the other; Flaubert, Mann, Newton, Falstaff.

concepts.label: Consubstantiality (ironic)
concepts.gloss: Simultaneously outside and within the other; foundation of true irony.

concepts.label: Peripety (A → non-A)
concepts.gloss: Strategic moment of reversal; the over-all ironic formula; basic pattern of drama and dialectic.

concepts.label: Internal fatality
concepts.gloss: True irony involves a principle of inevitability operating from within (though the extrinsic scene may contribute).

concepts.label: Primus inter pares character
concepts.gloss: Summarizing vessel / synecdochic representative of the development as a whole (Socrates in Plato; proletariat in Marx).

concepts.label: Adjectival / substantial duality
concepts.gloss: The most-representative character is both an adjectival qualifier and a substantial conclusion of the development.

concepts.label: Simplification of literalness
concepts.gloss: Third temptation of irony: collapsing the adjectival/substantial duality of the primus-inter-pares character.

concepts.label: Inter-transformability of tropes
concepts.gloss: Any trope fully developed generates the other three; the pairs overlap upon one another.

concepts.label: Trope as truth-apparatus
concepts.gloss: Burke's load-bearing reframing: tropes are not ornamental but constitutive of the discovery and description of 'the truth'.

concepts.label: Poetic vs. scientific behaviorism
concepts.gloss: Both translate spiritual to bodily; poet treats body as figure / symbolization, scientist treats body as real reduction.

concepts.label: Dramatic = dialectic equation
concepts.gloss: Where ideas are in action, drama; where agents are in ideation, dialectic — same structure, two phenomenologies.

concepts.label: Lex talionis (form-as-law)
concepts.gloss: Irony moves into the area of law and justice; form-as-anticipation-and-fulfilment in art parallels prophecy and prediction in history.

four_tropes.operational_gloss: Seeing one character (anything thinkable as distinct) in terms of another character; bringing out the thisness of a that. To consider A from the point of view of B is to use B as a perspective upon A. Reality is not dissolved by multi-perspectivism — it is established by it. Degrees of being correspond to variety-of-perspectives-supportable.
burke_examples: Human motivation considered in terms of conditioned reflexes / chemicals / class struggles / love of God / neurosis / pilgrimage / power / planetary motion / geography / sun spots (book p. 504)
17th-Century poet's 'conceit' as proto-perspective (book p. 504)
Lifting / smelling / tasting / tapping / holding-in-different-lights as multi-perspective establishment of an object's reality (book p. 504)
four_tropes.pentad_interaction: Most-implicates Agency (a perspective is the means-of-considering) and Scene (the chosen perspective re-scenes the act). Cross-cuts all five terms whenever the analyst chooses a frame of motives. Featured in Burke's diagnostic of philosophic schools: each school's featured pentad term is itself a metaphor / perspective on motivation.
four_tropes.dissertation_game_user_deployment: Cross-domain mapping in game-discourse: framing the player-as-consumer (economic metaphor), player-as-laborer (labor metaphor), player-as-co-author (literary metaphor), player-as-inhabitant (architectural metaphor), player-as-athlete (sport metaphor). Each is a perspective on the user-motive that selects different ratios for visibility; the dissertation can show that game-studies sub-schools (Aarseth's ergodic / Bogost's procedural / Calleja's incorporation / Sicart's play) feature different metaphor-perspectives on the user.

four_tropes.operational_gloss: Conveying an incorporeal or intangible state in terms of the corporeal or tangible. 'Heart' for 'emotions'; 'commotion' for emotion. All spiritual-realm vocabulary was metonymic in origin. Reduction is the one-direction (quality-to-quantity) special case: scientific realism's trope. Two senses must be tracked: the poet's metonymy as figure / symbolization, and the scientific behaviorist's metonymy as substantial reduction.
burke_examples: 'Heart' for 'emotions' (book p. 506)
I. A. Richards's substitution of 'commotion' for 'emotion' in Principles of Literary Criticism (book p. 506)
Western materialism's reduction of consciousness to motion (book p. 506)
Otto Neurath's isotypes (Modern Man in the Making) as reductive (quantitative) representations vs. realistic portrait painting (book p. 510)
Statistical surveys in sociology as fabulously-amassed reductive misrepresentations (book p. 510)
Korzybski's 'Structural Differential' (string, plugs, tin) as reductive 'way in' to meaning that predestines misrepresentation (book p. 511)
Thurman Arnold's psychiatric metaphor of social relations as reductive (book p. 511)
four_tropes.pentad_interaction: Most-implicates Agency (a reduction is a methodological apparatus) and Scene (the lower-order realm into which the higher is reduced). Decisively implicates Act when motive is reduced to behavior (poetic vs. scientific behaviorism). Operates the implicit cross-pentad collapse that produces materialist motive-accounts (Agent → Scene; Purpose → Agency).
four_tropes.dissertation_game_user_deployment: Player-reduced-to-scoreboard-number: KDA ratio, win rate, MMR, engagement minutes, retention curve, conversion funnel as metonymic reductions of player-motive to quantitative correlates. The dissertation can distinguish (a) telemetry-as-figure (the poet's use: numbers as symbolization of a quality whose substance lies elsewhere) from (b) telemetry-as-substantial-reduction (the scientific-behaviorist use: motive IS the number). This is the load-bearing methodological move for diagnosing 'gamification' rhetoric: gamification often deploys metonymy-as-real-reduction while claiming the warrants of metonymy-as-figure.

four_tropes.operational_gloss: Convertibility between two terms in an integral relationship: part for whole, whole for part, container for contained, sign for signified, material for thing made, cause for effect, genus for species, and all reversals. The 'noblest synecdoche' is microcosm-macrocosm identity (Leibniz). Two-way (unlike metonymy's one-way). Extended by Burke to cover before/after, implicit/explicit, temporal/logical sequence, name/narrative, disease/cure, hero/villain, active/passive.
burke_examples: Leibniz's monadology as grand-scale synecdoche; 'representation' is Leibniz's own word (book p. 508)
Rousseau's volonté générale as political-representation synecdoche (book p. 508)
Sensory representation: senses abstract size / shape / color / texture / weight from electro-chemical bundle we call a tree (book p. 508)
Artistic representation: internal synecdoche of the well-formed work (beginning contains close, close sums beginning) (book p. 508)
Coleridge's Ancient Mariner: 'the Albatross is a gerundive' — its nature when introduced is that-which-is-to-be-murdered; implicit contains future explicit (book p. 509)
Moby-Dick: Ahab as pursuer is pursued; his action is a passion (book p. 509)
four_tropes.pentad_interaction: Most-implicates Agent (the part-whole convertibility holds especially between an agent and the class / society / cosmos to which the agent belongs) and Purpose (the macrocosmic whole that the microcosmic part instantiates). Underwrites every representative-anecdote choice: which Act, Scene, Agent, Agency, or Purpose is held to stand-for the whole of human motivation? Each philosophic-school featuring is a synecdochic election.
four_tropes.dissertation_game_user_deployment: Avatar-stands-for-player (the canonical game-studies synecdoche): the controlled body in the game-world is part-for-whole representation of the user. Sub-deployments: party-stands-for-player (RPG); civilization-stands-for-player (4X); username-stands-for-player (multiplayer); screenshot/clip-stands-for-session (streaming culture); leaderboard-rank-stands-for-skill (esports). Each is a synecdoche the dissertation can analyze for representativeness (does the avatar truly represent the player, or does it reductively misrepresent — collapsing into metonymy?). The 'well-formed game session' is internally synecdochic in Burke's sense: tutorial contains endgame, endgame sums tutorial.

four_tropes.operational_gloss: Arises when one tries, by the interaction of terms upon one another, to produce a development that uses all the terms. From the standpoint of this total form (the 'perspective of perspectives'), no participating sub-perspective is precisely right or precisely wrong; all are voices, integrally affecting one another. True / classic / humble irony is grounded in consubstantiality with the 'enemy'; romantic / Pharisaic irony is grounded in superiority. The over-all formula: A returns as non-A (the peripety).
burke_examples: Allen Tate on Eliot's Waste Land seduction scene: Tate calls it humble irony; Burke calls it Pharisaic — the poet congratulates himself for not being like the petty clerk (book p. 513)
Newton observing the criminal: 'that man is going to prison for me' — true irony-and-humility, simultaneously outside and within the criminal (book p. 515)
Flaubert: 'Madame Bovary, c'est moi' as paradigm of consubstantial irony (book p. 514)
Thomas Mann's 'Judas psychology' (book p. 514)
Eliot's religious problem framed as converting romantic to classic irony — Murder in the Cathedral as ritual of motive-purification (book p. 514)
Falstaff (gloriously ironic) vs. Tartuffe (not ironic, pure hypocrite): Falstaff is consubstantial with his victim, Tartuffe merely simulates cooperation (book p. 515 footnote)
Engels: 'Without the slavery of antiquity, no modern socialism' — dialectic irony as technical equivalent of original sin (book p. 516)
Proletariat as 'the Socrates of the Marxist Symposium of History' — adjectival qualifier and substantial representative (book p. 516)
four_tropes.pentad_interaction: Implicates ALL FIVE pentad terms by structural definition: irony requires that all the terms (and agents) participate, none being precisely right or wrong. Operates on the ratios as a whole rather than on any individual term. Implicates Purpose most centrally in its peripety-formula (A → non-A) and Act in its peripety-as-reversal mechanic. The primus-inter-pares character (Socrates / proletariat) is itself a synecdochic election within the dialectic — irony folds back into synecdoche at the level of representative-character selection.
four_tropes.dissertation_game_user_deployment: Meta-gaming dialectic: the irony that the player who optimizes most ruthlessly for the designed objective often produces emergent behavior that subverts the design (speedrunning, glitch-exploitation, RMT, botting, grief-play, role-playing-against-roleplay). Burke's peripety-formula A → non-A maps directly onto game-design ironies: a difficulty curve designed to produce mastery (A) may return as toxic gatekeeping (non-A); a social system designed to foster cooperation (A) may return as harassment-vector (non-A); a reward economy designed to retain players (A) may return as compulsion-loop critique (non-A). The dissertation can deploy Burke's distinction between romantic / Pharisaic irony (the developer who treats the toxic player as 'not me') and classic / humble irony (the developer who recognizes consubstantiality — the toxic optimizer is the rational extension of the designed incentive).

positions.label: The four tropes are operations for the discovery and description of 'the truth', not figures of speech
positions.argument: Burke explicitly subordinates the figurative-usage tradition (Quintilian-Cicero-Richards-Ogden) to the literal-realistic usage. The four substitutions (perspective / reduction / representation / dialectic) are the load-bearing meanings; the figurative meanings are the inherited residue. This re-grounds the tropes as substantive analytical operations parallel to the pentad.

positions.label: The four tropes shade into one another; any one fully developed generates the other three
positions.argument: Burke's opening claim: 'Give a man but one of them, tell him to exploit its possibilities, and if he is thorough in doing so, he will come upon the other three.' Worked out structurally: dialectic gives representation by interacting perspectives, and the resulting perspective-of-perspectives is a reduction. Metonymy overlaps synecdoche overlaps metaphor overlaps irony — the essay's architecture exhibits the transitions.

positions.label: Metonymy / reduction is one-direction (quality-to-quantity); synecdoche / representation is two-direction
positions.argument: This is Burke's load-bearing asymmetry. Representation extends in either direction along the road between quality and quantity (and between any pair of integrally-related terms). Reduction follows only one direction. The footnote then re-broadens metonymy in the original sense (perspective-as-referring-back) to cover both directions — but the working / restricted sense holds the one-direction asymmetry firmly.

positions.label: True irony is humble and consubstantial; romantic irony is Pharisaic and superior — and only the first deserves the name
positions.argument: Burke devotes the central middle of section IV to this distinction, with Tate's reading of Eliot as the negative exemplum and Newton-Flaubert-Mann-Falstaff as positive exempla. The dialectic of irony requires that the analyst be 'simultaneously both outside the criminal and within him'. Romantic irony — the artist superior to the rejected role — is a poetic attitude, not the poetic attitude.

positions.label: A terminology of conceptual analysis must be built on a representative anecdote, not a reductive one
positions.argument: Burke's methodological hinge between sections III and IV. The scientist who builds his motivation-vocabulary around a laboratory rat-experiment and then transfers it to adult human acts has misrepresented the higher-order case as a debunking. Korzybski's Structural Differential and Arnold's psychiatric metaphor are named instances. The principle generalizes: any 'way in' to a subject must be representative, not merely reductively-tractable.

philosophers_cited.use: Monadology as the grand-scale paradigm of synecdochic identity; 'representation' is Leibniz's own word for this synecdochic relationship.

philosophers_cited.name: Rousseau
philosophers_cited.use: Volonté générale as paradigm of political-representation synecdoche.

philosophers_cited.name: Marx (/ Marxism)

philosophers_cited.name: Engels
philosophers_cited.use: Direct quotation on slavery and modern socialism — dialectic irony / technical equivalent of original sin.

philosophers_cited.name: Plato (Socrates)
philosophers_cited.use: Socrates as primus-inter-pares in the Platonic dialogue — both adjectival qualifier and substantial representative. Socratic irony as dramatic.

philosophers_cited.name: Aristotle (background)
philosophers_cited.use: Implicit: peripety as Aristotelian dramatic structure (Poetics) imported into the dialectic / irony equation.

philosophers_cited.name: Hegel (background)
philosophers_cited.use: Implicit: dialectic-as-transformation-of-terms imported but used in the 'restricted sense'; the broader Hegelian sense is acknowledged in the opening footnote.

literary_examples.author: Coleridge
literary_examples.burke_reading: The Albatross is a gerundive: its nature when introduced is that-which-is-to-be-murdered; implicit contains the future explicit.

literary_examples.author: Melville
literary_examples.burke_reading: Ahab as pursuer is pursued; his action is a passion — synecdochic reversal of active and passive.

literary_examples.author: T. S. Eliot
literary_examples.burke_reading: Tate reads the scene as humble irony; Burke reads it as 'thank God I am not like other men' — Pharisaic, not consubstantial.

literary_examples.author: T. S. Eliot
literary_examples.burke_reading: Ritual aimed at purification of motives — converting romantic to classic irony.

literary_examples.author: Flaubert
literary_examples.burke_reading: 'Madame Bovary, c'est moi' — paradigm of consubstantial / classic irony.

literary_examples.author: Thomas Mann
literary_examples.burke_reading: The applied 'Judas psychology' as recognition that the analyst contains the betrayer.

literary_examples.author: Shakespeare
literary_examples.burke_reading: Falstaff identifies with his victim; converts 'thine' through 'ours' into 'mine' via convivial / sociality / religious sympathetic distortion.

literary_examples.author: Molière
literary_examples.burke_reading: Tartuffe is the contrast case: exploits cooperative values for competitive ends, but uses piety as mere deception — competition simulating cooperation.

literary_examples.author: Anatole France
literary_examples.burke_reading: At least a humility of gentle surrender, if not the humility of strength.

interlocutors.name: Allen Tate
interlocutors.engagement: PRIMARY antagonist of this essay (the only sustained polemic of Appendix D). Tate is quoted at length on Eliot's Waste Land seduction scene as exemplar of irony-as-humility; Burke refutes by arguing the passage is Pharisaic, not humble. Tate's definition of irony ('that arrangement of experience... which permits to the spectator an insight superior to that of the actor') is taken as the formulation of romantic irony, against which Burke's classic / humble irony is opposed.

interlocutors.name: Cleanth Brooks
interlocutors.engagement: Cited approvingly for the observation that the very absence of irony in relativism makes it maximally susceptible to irony (the monologic absolutism that is its own peripety).

interlocutors.name: I. A. Richards
interlocutors.engagement: Cited approvingly: 'commotion' for 'emotion' in Principles of Literary Criticism — quietly metonymic, exemplifying the poet's archaicizing use of metonymy.

interlocutors.name: Otto Neurath
interlocutors.engagement: Cited critically: Neurath's isotypes (Modern Man in the Making) as reductive representations contrasted with realistic portrait painting — also cross-referenced to Burke's own review 'Quantity and Quality' in The Philosophy of Literary Form.

interlocutors.name: Alfred Korzybski
interlocutors.engagement: Cited critically: the 'Structural Differential' (contraption of string, plugs, and tin) as a reductive 'way in' to the analysis of meaning that predestines misrepresentation.

interlocutors.name: Thurman Arnold
interlocutors.engagement: Cited critically: reduction of social relations to terms of the psychiatric metaphor as a parallel methodological error.

interlocutors.name: Rhetorical-figure tradition (Quintilian, Cicero, modern)
interlocutors.engagement: Implicit interlocutor: Burke subordinates the entire figurative-usage tradition to the literal-realistic usage of the four tropes. This is the silent re-grounding that justifies the essay's existence as parallel apparatus to the pentad.

interlocutors.name: Hayden-White-style trope theory (anticipated)
interlocutors.engagement: Anticipated rather than engaged — White's Metahistory (1973) postdates by 28 years. The four-tropes apparatus here directly prefigures White's metahistorical typology of historians by trope; the dissertation can flag this as a precursor relationship.

tensions.label: Restricted-sense vs. broad-sense dialectic
tensions.description: In the opening footnote Burke notes that 'dialectic' is here used in the restricted sense — the trope-partner of irony — while in the broader sense all four transformations are themselves dialectical. This creates an internal pressure: dialectic is both one trope-pair (= irony) AND the meta-operation by which all four trope-pairs operate. The pressure is productive — it shows that irony is the meta-trope, the trope-of-tropes, the perspective of perspectives applied to the trope-apparatus itself.

tensions.label: Restricted (one-direction) vs. broader (two-direction) sense of metonymy / reduction
tensions.description: Burke first asserts reduction-as-metonymy follows the road from quality to quantity in one direction only (vs. synecdoche's two-direction relation). The footnote at book p. 509 then admits that originally 'reduction' meant 'referring-back' and could go in any direction — anything considered in terms of anything else is a 'reduction' in this original sense, which makes reduction approach perspective / metaphor again. The one-direction working-sense vs. the two-direction original-sense produces an internal tension that the essay resolves by keeping the restricted sense as operative.

tensions.label: True irony is humble, but irony tempts toward Pharisaic superiority
tensions.description: Section IV catalogues three temptations of irony (relativism / Pharisaic-superiority / simplification-of-literalness). The Pharisaic temptation is the load-bearing one because the very structure of irony — the standpoint above the participating sub-perspectives — naturally invites the analyst to feel superior. Burke's resolution is consubstantiality: the analyst must be both outside and within. The tension is permanent and methodologically generative.

tensions.label: Every analytical terminology is built on some anecdote; how to know it is representative rather than reductive?
tensions.description: Burke's diagnostic principle — that conceptual terminologies must be built on representative anecdotes — is itself a methodological hazard. The criterion of representativeness is internal to the trope-apparatus (a representative anecdote is one whose synecdoche genuinely converts between part and whole) and so cannot be settled outside it. This is a productive circularity rather than a vicious one, but it bears flagging.

tensions.label: Is the tropological apparatus parallel to the pentad, or subordinate to it?
tensions.description: Appendix D's placement (an Appendix, not a Part) suggests subordination, but its content — a complete and self-standing analytical apparatus that cross-cuts every pentad term — operates as a parallel apparatus. The plan correctly locks it as 'full unit' with its own standalone Phase 3 synthesis. The tension is resolved in this pipeline by treating the tropes as the dialectical-rhetorical operations the pentad terms undergo, not as a competing fivefold-vs-fourfold typology.

metaphor_perspective.Act: Choosing the verb-frame (an act seen as conquest is seen-from-conquest-as-perspective)
metaphor_perspective.Scene: Choosing the circumference (scene seen as marketplace vs. battlefield vs. classroom)
metaphor_perspective.Agent: Choosing the agent-type-as-frame (agent seen as consumer / citizen / believer)
metaphor_perspective.Agency: Choosing the instrument-as-frame (means seen as tool vs. obstacle vs. ritual)
metaphor_perspective.Purpose: Choosing the end-as-frame (purpose seen as profit vs. salvation vs. mastery)

metonymy_reduction.Act: Reducing act to behavior (poetic vs. scientific behaviorism, book p. 506)
metonymy_reduction.Agent: Reducing agent to body / biology / demographics
metonymy_reduction.Purpose: Reducing purpose to quantifiable goal-state (the one-direction quality-to-quantity move)

synecdoche_representation.Act: Election of one act as standing-for-all-acts (representative-anecdote choice)
synecdoche_representation.Scene: Microcosm-macrocosm: a scene-fragment representing the cosmos (Leibniz)
synecdoche_representation.Agency: An instrument representing the order it instantiates (the cross representing salvation)
synecdoche_representation.Purpose: An end-state representing the developmental whole (the primus-inter-pares character)

irony_dialectic.Act: Peripety: A → non-A; the act returns as its reversal
irony_dialectic.Scene: Scene reframed by the perspective of perspectives
irony_dialectic.Agent: Consubstantiality with the 'enemy' agent (Flaubert / Newton / Falstaff)
irony_dialectic.Agency: Dialectical interaction of means producing emergent unintended results
irony_dialectic.Purpose: Internal fatality: the purpose that arose in time perishes in time, and the developments leading to its rise lead to its fall

trope_pentad_interaction_matrix.note: Burke does not lay out this matrix explicitly, but every trope-pair operation in the essay is also a pentad-term operation. The matrix is the Phase-2 analytical extension that makes the parallel-apparatus claim concrete; the Phase-3 manual deliverable will work each cell.

cross_pipeline_bridges.bridge: The pentad statement (Introduction) is the analytical apparatus the tropes operate upon.
Scene-as-container is a synecdoche (container-for-contained); the master spatial metaphor of GM-01 is itself a metaphor / perspective on motive.
The paradox of substance is a paradox of synecdoche (the substantial whole vs. the parts that represent it).
Scope-and-reduction is the explicit foreshadowing of GM-13's metonymy-as-reduction; the representative-anecdote concept appears in both units.

Each philosophic school featured in Part 2 features its pentad term via a particular trope: materialism features Scene via metonymy / reduction; idealism features Agent via metaphor / perspective; realism features Act via synecdoche / representation (Aristotle's actus); pragmatism features Agency via metonymy; mysticism features Purpose via synecdoche (microcosm-macrocosm).
Dialectic in General is the operational expansion of trope-IV; the transformation-of-terms IS the trope-apparatus at work.
The Keats and Moore appendices are worked synecdochic / ironic analyses of poems — instances of the tropological apparatus in action.
Calleja's incorporation thesis maps onto Burke's consubstantiality: the player is simultaneously inside and outside the gameworld — a structural irony in Burke's classic sense.
Burke's metaphor-as-perspective parallels phantasia-as-presentational: both are operations of seeing-as. The dissertation can use the pairing to bridge classical and dramatistic vocabularies.
Discomfort-as-peripety: the uncomfortable situation is the moment where A returns as non-A in the user's lived experience.

dissertation_deployment_summary: The four-trope apparatus is the dissertation's primary lens for distinguishing how game-discourse constructs the user-motive. Each trope underwrites a recognizable discourse-regime: metaphor (cross-domain framing — gamification rhetoric and skeuomorphic ports of work / school / fitness into 'play'); metonymy (telemetric reduction — the player as KDA / MMR / retention-curve / conversion-funnel); synecdoche (avatar / leaderboard / clip as representative part-for-whole); irony (meta-gaming, speedrunning, glitch-exploitation, emergent-play, the consubstantiality of designer and exploiter). The dissertation will deploy these as a parallel apparatus to the pentad: each user-motive analysis names both its featured pentad term and its featured trope-operation, yielding a five-by-four cell matrix the chapter argument moves through. Burke's classic-vs-romantic-irony distinction is the load-bearing methodological move for the dissertation's critique of developer / academic discourse about 'toxic' or 'whale' players: a developer who treats the toxic optimizer as 'not me' deploys romantic irony; a developer who recognizes consubstantiality — that the toxic optimizer is the rational extension of the designed incentive — deploys classic irony. The pipeline thus equips the dissertation with both a typology (the four tropes) and a normative criterion (consubstantial irony as the diagnostic of good faith).
